newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat falls on planting progress.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat falls on planting progress.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures dropped sharply on Tuesday pressured by spring wheat planting progress in parts of the Northern Plains and spillover bearish sentiment, traders said.
USDA on Monday said that as of Sunday, 13 percent of U.S. spring wheat had been planted, up from five percent a week earlier but behind 21 percent a year ago.
"We are just following the other two markets," one trader said, referring to the declines in KCBT and CBOT wheat futures.
He noted good rains in France and seeding progress over the weekend in parts of the Northern Plains.
French wheat prices eased on Monday on improved prospects for the 1997 harvest after the weekend's rain and forcasts for more rain and cooler temperatures in the next few days.
Volume was thin amid scattered commission-house type selling, the trader said.
At 1007 CDT, MGE July wheat lost eight cents at $4.18 a bushel while the rest of the board was six to 6-3/4 cents lower.
